title: Sita changes Rama's mind
hook: Rama lists the forest's dangers, Sita answers every one, and he gives way; why devotees say Sita-Ram
carry: Sita-Ram: never one without the other
tomorrow: not everyone is calm. what will Lakshmana say?

segments.voice: Yesterday: Sita's argument began. If you're sent to the forest, so am I: a partner in dharma shares the road. Today Rama tries again, and so does she.
screen: `A PARTNER IN DHARMA SHARES THE ROAD.`

segments.voice: How do you stop someone you love from following you into danger, without forbidding it? Rama tries a list: every hardship the forest holds, one by one. It's love, mostly, and also a way of winning without saying no. He has watched his father break and his mother weep today, and he wants one person he loves kept safe. He means every word. And Sita, who has been patient, runs out of patience.
screen: `THE LIST OF DANGERS.` → `WINNING WITHOUT SAYING NO.` → `SITA LOSES HER PATIENCE.`

segments.voice: The forest is hard, Rama says. Lions roar from mountain caves. Rivers are full of crocodiles. You sleep on fallen leaves and eat whatever fruit you find, or nothing. Wind, darkness, hunger, snakes, thorns. Stay here. Sita answers his list item by item. With you, the grass will feel like a soft blanket; the fruit you bring me will taste like nectar. And when I was a girl, people who read the signs told my family I would one day live in a forest. Still Rama hesitates, and she stings. What was my father thinking, she asks, when he chose as his son-in-law a woman in the form of a man? Valmiki doesn't soften it. She's accusing Rama of failing at the one thing a protector is for: keeping her with him. Then she weeps. And Rama gives way. He holds her. I didn't know your mind, he says. I wouldn't want heaven itself without you. Come with me. In a story about a son obeying his father without a question, the wife questions, pushes, and changes her husband's mind. And this is why, in Hindu devotion, Rama is almost never alone. Temples and home shrines show Sita beside him. Devotees chant Sita-Ram, her name first, and many greet each other with Jai Siya Ram. Some traditions teach that you come to God through the Goddess at his side; that's a reading. The text says it plainer: he didn't want heaven without her.
screen: `LIONS, CROCODILES, THORNS.` · `A WOMAN IN THE FORM OF A MAN?` · `I DIDN'T KNOW YOUR MIND. COME.` · `SITA-RAM: HER NAME FIRST.` · then, large: `NEVER ONE WITHOUT THE OTHER.`

segments.voice: Try a practice many Hindus keep: japa, repeating a holy name. Breathe in, and silently say Sita; breathe out, and say Ram. Let the two names travel together, the way the two of them did. If you don't pray, breathe in on with, out on together, and think of someone you'd walk a hard road beside.
Sita's argument, won. She answers every danger, rebukes Rama sharply, and he relents: I didn't know your mind; come with me.
Hold on to it: Sita-Ram, never one without the other. Tomorrow, someone in the palace isn't calm at all. That's day five hundred twenty-seven.

howItsDone: Rama is rarely shown alone: temples and home shrines picture him with Sita, and devotees chant Sita-Ram and greet each other with Jai Siya Ram, her name first.

fork.setup: you're Rama. your wife has answered every danger you named and wept. what do you do?
options: insist she stay; it's for her own good.
send her to her father's house.
admit you didn't know her mind, and take her.

original.note: Sanskrit vanavāsa: forest-dwelling, exile in the forest; vana (forest) plus vāsa (living).

trapdoor: what you thought: Rama decided to take Sita.
what it means: she argued, rebuked him sharply, and changed his mind.
what a scholar hears: Sita's rebuke, asking what her father was thinking when he took a woman in a man's form as son-in-law, questions Rama's very manhood, and Valmiki leaves it unsoftened.

chat.says: nani wrote diya a goodbye card and signed it 'jai siya ram'. why is sita's name in it? i thought it was rama's thing
options: Rama's never alone in devotion. Sita wouldn't stay behind, and he said heaven without her wasn't worth it: Siya-Ram.
it's just a rhyme. the name doesn't mean anything.
Sita's in it because she's Rama's servant.
chat.meaning: Sita won her place beside Rama; he wouldn't want heaven without her. So devotees say Sita-Ram, or Jai Siya Ram: never one without the other.

tie.story: Sita answered every danger Rama named until he said he wouldn't want heaven without her.
tie.friend: Priya can see why Nani's card names Sita first: in devotion Rama is never without her, the way Diya isn't going alone.
tie.you: whose name do you always say together with yours?
